In the field

Make the most of your next gem show.

Black Michael Collection · November 09, 2026

How to prepare for a gem and mineral show, compare pieces thoughtfully, and keep the details that matter.

Arrive with a short wish list

Write down the kinds of pieces you hope to see and a comfortable budget. Include sizes or jewelry measurements if relevant. A little preparation gives you a starting point while leaving room for an unexpected discovery.

Use the opportunity to look closely

Seeing a piece in person lets you ask questions while it is in front of you. Ask permission before handling specimens or jewelry, and follow the vendor’s instructions. Take time to look from several angles.

Keep a note of the piece

With the vendor’s permission, photograph the piece and its label together. Note the booth, asking price and the questions you discussed. This makes it easier to return to the right vendor after walking the show.

Talk through the details

Ask what is known about the piece, what information supports the description, and whether any documentation is included. Confirm what you will receive and the terms of the purchase before making a decision.

Plan the journey home

Ask how to pack and transport your purchase. Keep the seller’s contact information and receipt with your collection records. If you need time to decide, ask whether a hold is possible rather than assuming the item will remain available.
